 CNN to launch new election data and analysis tool to demystify Decision Desk
 Sara Fischer Updated Fri, October 23, 2026 at 2:52 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. CNN broadcasts on election night on Nov. 6, 2024. Photo: Laurent Caron/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images CNN will debut a new election data and analysis tool called Sightline that gives political junkies access to the expertise behind its Decision Desk.
 Why it matters: Sightline aims to pull back the curtain on the real-time metrics and logic that power the network's forecasts.
 "I think there's long been a desire to better explain what it is that's happening within a decision desk operation," CNN's vice president of election and data reporting Jennifer Agiesta said.
 "It seems like this magical wizardry," but "there's math here."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Zoom in: Sightline will be available on CNN's homepage and app beginning Nov. 3. It will also be featured throughout the network's "Election Night in America" broadcast.
 The tool will only include data and analysis across key Senate and gubernatorial contests nationwide — no House races.
 Anyone can view high-level race assessments online for free. CNN digital subscribers can access deeper data analysis and visualizations, including county-level data breakdowns and vote-method splits.
 How it works: Sightline assesses races across five metrics: including outstanding votes, geographical voting patterns, voting methods, historical voting patterns and the size of a race lead.
 Those indicators feed into real-time assessment of each race, which can be categorized as "Highly Favors D," "Favors D," "Neutral," "Favors R" and "Highly Favors R," Agiesta said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Zoom out: The product, which isn't sponsored, is meant to enhance CNN's linear TV coverage while driving audience engagement online that can be funneled into CNN's paid subscription offerings.
 The big picture: News and prediction market companies are expanding election offerings to hyper-serve political fanatics seeking detailed data and analysis.
 CBS News is launching a new election night streaming show called "The Nerd Show" that gives political junkies the opportunity to watch its decision desk analyze races and make calls in real time.
 NBC News is launching a cross-platform franchise centered on Steve Kornacki's signature data-driven analysis.
